name: TIG Rotator Controls
tagline: Low-voltage control wiring for the ESP32-P4 TIG welding rotator
summary: The low-voltage controller subsystem of the DIY TIG welding positioner: the GUITION JC4880P443C ESP32-P4 touch board, its speed pot, direction switch, foot pedal (switch plus ADS1115 pot), conditioned E-STOP input and the DM542T signal terminal. Motor power, the stepper, gearbox and the grounded metal enclosure are outside this package.

connections.why: Driver alarm back to the controller
Alarm return on the same ground
Common ground with the driver logic
Switch pulls the input to ground
Shares the touch I2C data line
Shares the touch I2C clock line
Pedal pot wiper to the ADC

firmware.behaviour: Bring-up only for this test. The real firmware is the repository's src/ tree (FreeRTOS, LVGL 9, FastAccelStepper on RMT, E-STOP ISR on PIN_ESTOP FALLING). ENA must stay HIGH (inhibit) at boot; never pulse STEP from a bring-up test.

showcase.headline: Steady rotation for one-handed TIG welds.
showcase.subhead: The control box wiring for an ESP32-P4 welding rotator: speed pot, direction switch, foot pedal and a supervised E-STOP input, generated from one project file.

howItWorks.title: Set the speed
howItWorks.body: Turn the pot or tap the touch screen. The rotator holds the surface speed you chose.

howItWorks.title: Start with your foot
howItWorks.body: Press the pedal to start and let go to stop, so both hands stay on the torch and filler.

howItWorks.title: Stop through the driver
howItWorks.body: The E-STOP input and the driver alarm make the firmware stop pulses and inhibit ENA, and need a reset before it runs again. This path goes through the controller and does not disconnect motor power.

features.title: One pin map
features.body: The wiring guide and the firmware pin header come from the same file, so GPIO numbers cannot drift apart.

features.title: Driver alarm wired
features.body: The DM542T alarm output is read back, so a driver that reports a fault (over-current, over-voltage) stops the job. It cannot see a stall without an encoder.

features.title: Pedal on its own ADC
features.body: An ADS1115 on the touch I2C bus reads the pedal pot, leaving the board ADC for the panel pot.

features.title: Built for HF
features.body: Everything lives in one grounded metal enclosure with the driver and PSU, which TIG HF start requires.

faq.q: Can I print a plastic case for this?
faq.a: No. TIG HF start needs the controller, driver and PSU in one grounded metal enclosure. This package leaves the enclosure out on purpose.

faq.q: Is the E-STOP a safety circuit?
faq.a: No. It is a supervised input on GPIO34 that the firmware acts on through ENA. It is not independent of the controller and does not cut motor power. Verify pressed, released, broken wire and power loss against docs/estop_timing.md before use.
The firmware and pin map have run on the owner's machine (v2.3.1). This generated guide has not been followed by anyone yet; check each step against HARDWARE_SETUP.md.

faq.q: Can the ESP32-P4 drive the DM542T directly?
faq.a: Only if your driver's input specification allows 3.3 V drive. The checker flags it as marginal; use a level interface if the manual asks for 5 V signals.
